claims.claim: Gradient-boosted tree ensembles mostly outperform 11 deep learning approaches across five real-world tabular datasets.
claims.quote: algorithms based on gradient-boosted tree ensembles still mostly outperform

claims.claim: Tree-based models remain state-of-the-art on medium-sized data (~10K samples) even without accounting for their superior speed.
claims.quote: Results show that tree-based models remain state-of-the-art on medium-sized data (~10K samples) even without accounting for their superior speed.

claims.claim: The study conducted a 20,000 compute hours hyperparameter search for each learner across 45 datasets.
claims.quote: every point of a 20 000 compute hours hyperparameter search for each learner

claims.claim: For many datasets, performance difference between GBDTs and NNs is negligible, or light hyperparameter tuning on a GBDT is more important than choosing between NNs and GBDTs.
claims.quote: for a surprisingly high number of datasets, either the performance difference between GBDTs and NNs is negligible, or light hyperparameter tuning on a GBDT is more important than choosing between NNs and GBDTs

claims.claim: GBDTs are much better than NNs at handling skewed or heavy-tailed feature distributions and other dataset irregularities.
claims.quote: GBDTs are much better than NNs at handling skewed or heavy-tailed feature distributions and other forms of dataset irregularities

claims.claim: Tree-based models remain state-of-the-art on medium-sized data (∼10K samples) even without accounting for their superior speed.
claims.quote: Results show that tree-based models remain state-of-the-art on medium-sized data (∼10K samples) even without accounting for their superior speed

claims.claim: The benchmark includes a 20,000 compute hours hyperparameter search for each learner across 48 datasets.
claims.quote: every point of a 20 000 compute hours hyperparameter search for each learner

claims.claim: Well-regularized plain MLPs significantly outperform recent specialized neural architectures and even outperform strong traditional ML methods such as XGBoost.
claims.quote: well-regularized plain MLPs significantly outperform recent state-of-the-art specialized neural network architectures, and (ii) they even outperform strong traditional ML methods, such as XGBoost

claims.claim: XGBoost generally achieves the best predictive performance among gradient boosting variants for QSAR modeling.
claims.quote: Our results show that XGBoost generally achieves the best predictive performance

claims.claim: The relevance of each hyperparameter varies greatly across datasets and optimizing as many hyperparameters as possible is crucial to maximize predictive performance.
claims.quote: the relevance of each hyperparameter varies greatly across datasets and that it is crucial to optimize as many hyperparameters as possible to maximize the predictive performance

claims.claim: RealMLP offers a favorable time-accuracy tradeoff compared to other neural baselines and is competitive with GBDTs in benchmark scores on medium-to-large tabular datasets.
claims.quote: RealMLP offers a favorable time-accuracy tradeoff compared to other neural baselines and is competitive with GBDTs in terms of benchmark scores

claims.claim: A combination of RealMLP and GBDTs with improved default parameters can achieve excellent results without hyperparameter tuning.
claims.quote: a combination of RealMLP and GBDTs with improved default parameters can achieve excellent results without hyperparameter tuning

claims.claim: The proposed GNN model achieves competitive results when compared to boosted-tree solutions on seven public datasets.
claims.quote: achieving competitive results when compared to boosted-tree solutions

claims.claim: TabPFN-2.5 Scaling Mode shows no evidence of the performance gap to gradient boosting shrinking as datasets scale up to 10M rows.
claims.quote: No evidence of the performance gap to gradient boosting shrinking as we scale up

open_questions: How do tuned GBDTs compare to well-tuned MLPs and linear models specifically (not just specialized neural architectures)?
What is the minimal tuning budget needed for GBDTs to reach peak performance on typical tabular benchmarks?
How does the relative performance change on very large datasets (>1M rows) where TabPFN Scaling Mode and GBDTs are both evaluated?
Do linear models with proper feature engineering and regularization close the gap to GBDTs on structured tabular data?
